newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish elections in September 1998 - govt source.
newsitem.headline: Danish elections in September 1998 - govt source.

text.p: Danish Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen, his ruling coalition lagging in opinion polls, expects to hold a general election on schedule in September 1998, a government source told Reuters on Monday.

He said that a weekend Social Democratic Party conference agreed that local authority elections this November, an expected EU referendum in May 1998 and the absence of many voters during the summer meant that elections would be best held shortly before the current mandate expires on September 21 next year.

Latest opinion polls put the opposition Conservative-Liberal alliance ahead of the ruling centre-left coalition but with both sides, as usual, depending on sometimes volatile far-left and far-right opposition parties for their majority.
There has not been a single-party, majority government in Denmark since 1909.

A Greens poll concluded on August 6 gave the current Social Democrat-Radical Liberal government 32.4 percent of the vote if an election were held immediately and the Conservative-Liberal challengers 43.1 percent.
An August 4 Sonar survey gave the centre-left 34.4 percent and the right 41.7 percent.

The right's position would be boosted if the Centre Democrats (CD), who left the Rasmussen government last December in protest at its increasing reliance on the far left, join a centre-right coalition next time round.
There is some speculation that they could be joined by the Radical Liberals, who are openly uncomfortable with Rasmussen.
Some polls have predicted the CD itself might fail to meet the two percent threshold for entering parliament. Both the latest polls gave the CD 2.2 percent.
